clue.text: Article on one uncontrollable movement in a vote linked to no party

indicators.note: in tells us the one-plus-twitch-plus-article group sits inside the words a vote

parts.note: a poll is a vote

indicators.note: on here means the article is attached after the preceding pieces, as in an across entry

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a tic is an involuntary twitch
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone describes a twitchy, unaffiliated voter casting a ballot without party ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' suggests a political movement, but it is a twitch; 'on' attaches the article after one and the twitch, and that group sits within the poll.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apolitical means having no political allegiance, so it is a synonym of being tied to no party.

clue.text: Oriental leader of party needing special Asian kit

indicators.note: leader of picks out the opening letter of the following word
special suggests the letters are put into an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A party chief from the East needs specially made Asian clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges ASIANKIT into AKISTANI after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani comes from South Asia, so in the old broad sense is Oriental, an Easterner.

clue.text: Don't take a holiday

definitions.meaning: to ... something is not to take it

explanation.definitionFit: To leave something is to refrain from taking it; leave is also authorised absence from work.

clue.text: Matching collection

parts.note: matching here means marrying: the clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage

explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and household linen a bride collects before her wedding.

clue.text: Appreciative member of audience giving tongue

definitions.meaning: the metal striker inside a bell is called its tongue

explanation.definitionFit: One who claps applauds a show; the clapper is also the tongue inside a bell.

clue.text: Administered a beating with extra spirit

definitions.meaning: to lace someone is to thrash them
a ... drink has had alcohol added

explanation.definitionFit: Laced can mean thrashed, and also describes a drink spiked with added liquor.

clue.text: Get ready for a future queen, possibly

definitions.meaning: to ... an item is to get ready money (cash) for it at a pawnbroker
in chess a ... reaching the far rank may be promoted to a queen

explanation.definitionFit: Pawning raises ready cash; a chess pawn can be promoted to become a queen.

clue.text: Piano, on signal arranged, accompanied vocal music? No

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano (softly)

indicators.note: arranged, a musical word here, tells us to put the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A pianist arranges music at a signal, though the song is unaccompanied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns ONSIGNAL into LAINSONG after P. The '? No' says the definition is the opposite: plainsong is unaccompanied chant.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied monophonic church chant, so it is vocal music that is not accompanied.

clue.text: One who goes to court gets nothing in trial right

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the word for trouble

parts.note: a trial is an affliction or woe
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A defendant ends up in court with nothing to show from his trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal, but it means woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them romantically, so a suitor is one who courts.

clue.text: It's OK to abbreviate it

parts.note: OK is the standard postal abbreviation of a particular US state, so it is quite all right to shorten that state's name to OK

explanation.definitionFit: OK is the official two-letter postal code for this American state.

clue.text: He provided bank transfers for late clients

definitions.text: He provided bank transfers for late clients

parts.words: He provided bank transfers for late clients
parts.note: reads like a banker, but means the mythical ferryman carrying the dead (late) across the river Styx from one bank to the other

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ferryman rowed the souls of the dead across the Styx.

clue.text: Put ratings on a couple of vessels carrying drug

indicators.note: carrying means the pair of vessel abbreviations holds the drug within them
couple of asks for the vessel abbreviation twice

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Inspectors grade a pair of ships found smuggling narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or rate, as in putting a rating or value on property.

clue.text: Fastidiousness shown by leading journalist in food store

indicators.note: in places the senior newspaper figure inside the larder

parts.note: a pantry is a small room for storing food
ED, short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A fussy editor is spotted rummaging in the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor details, a close synonym of fussy fastidiousness.

clue.text: Royal portraitist showing, prince with son

parts.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A court painter displays a royal prince alongside his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal' only colours the surface, making 'prince' feel like part of a royal sitting; Frans Hals was a Dutch portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frans Hals was a famous seventeenth-century Dutch painter of portraits such as The Laughing Cavalier.

clue.text: Pupil in swimming group joining club to play, ultimately

parts.note: a school is a group of fish

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A pupil in the swimming team also joins a drama club.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolboy is a boy attending school, hence a pupil.

clue.text: Disorder cost a ruler a bit of capital

indicators.note: Disorder is an imperative telling us to jumble the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A ruler's chaotic reign has cost him a slice of his capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLS COURT is a district of west London, hence a bit of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl's Court is a district within London, so it is part of the British capital.

clue.text: Where performers, ultimately, are barely visible

definitions.text: Where performers, ultimately, are barely visible

parts.words: Where performers, ultimately, are barely visible
parts.note: barely means almost unclothed: a venue where entertainers end up undressed

explanation.definitionFit: At a strip club performers undress, so by the end of their act they are barely clothed.

clue.text: Combination of blues for vessels in service

parts.note: royal blue is one shade of blue
navy blue is another shade of blue

explanation.surface: Mixing two shades of blue for the uniform of serving ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Navy is Britain's naval service, its fleet of ships in service.

clue.text: Oxford Street knitwear for an athlete

parts.note: the main street of Oxford is known simply as the High
a jumper is a knitted pullover sweater

explanation.surface: A runner shops for a sweater on Oxford's main shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford Street' looks like the London shopping street, but it means the High in the city of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A high jumper is a track-and-field competitor, one kind of athlete.

clue.text: With cast selected, play one's part

parts.note: to pitch is to throw or cast
a player picked for the team is in

explanation.surface: Now the cast is chosen, each actor must play their role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' and 'play' both suggest theatre, but cast means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in is to join in and contribute one's share, an idiom for doing one's part.

clue.text: Artist's year in Indian state

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for year inside the Indian state's name

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast

explanation.surface: A painter spends a year living in Goa.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Conceited way Mussorgsky introduced himself?

definitions.meaning: full of oneself, the opposite of humble
the composer's first name was Modest

explanation.definitionFit: Immodest means boastful or vain, a synonym of conceited; split up it gives the composer's introduction.

clue.text: Using one motorway, end up in US city

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, means the word for goal is written from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A driver takes the M1 and finishes up in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AIM to MIA; MI is the M1, London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large city in Florida, in the United States.

clue.text: Taken out of context rather unusually

indicators.note: Taken out of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark is quoted out of context in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra used as an adverb means especially or unusually, as in extra careful.

clue.text: Fare for Spaniard to hop back to US city

indicators.note: back says the jump word is read in reverse

parts.note: to hop is to leap
LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A Spanish traveller hops back to Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish, so it is food (fare) for a Spaniard.

clue.text: Lady of the lake, originally English

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The Lady of the Lake was English in origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady of the lake' evokes Arthurian legend, but 'Lady' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's name, so a lady.

clue.text: Opening manoeuvre in school scrap

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
a bit is a scrap or small piece

explanation.surface: A playground fight starts with a clever opening move.
explanation.walkthrough: GAM, a school of whales, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move in chess, sacrificing material for advantage.

clue.text: Port that gives rise to divine thoughts?

definitions.meaning: a harbour town; this one is on Anglesey in Wales

definitions.text: that gives rise to divine thoughts?
definitions.meaning: read as a sacred mind or saintly brain, the source of pious thinking

explanation.definitionFit: Holyhead is a ferry port in north Wales; split, it suggests a saintly mind full of divine thoughts.

clue.text: She's not a field worker, according to Matthew

definitions.text: She's not a field worker, according to Matthew

parts.words: She's not a field worker, according to Matthew
parts.note: St Matthew's gospel says the flowers of the field toil not, neither do they spin; 'She' suggests a woman's name

explanation.definitionFit: Matthew 6:28 says to consider these flowers of the field, which neither toil nor spin, and it is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Ennoble any characters following special order of queen

indicators.note: the letters of the two preceding words are put into a new special order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Ennobling anyone follows a special decree of the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn was the second wife of Henry VIII and so a queen of England.
